expectations.text: States that no ISO, IAB, or equivalent external body certifies marketplace listing quality
expectations.evidence: "No ISO, IAB or equivalent body certifies marketplace listing quality."

expectations.text: Refuses the 'Certified Listings' claim as written, because it implies an external certification that does not exist
expectations.evidence: "'Certified Listings' implies an external certification, which is an unverifiable claim"; rename the claim.

expectations.text: Offers the compositional alternative naming three components and naming it as Tidewell's own program: WCAG for accessibility, recognized security attestations for security posture, and Tidewell's own published rubric for content
expectations.evidence: Table: Security (own review plus recognized attestations), Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA), Content (own published rubric); "named as Tidewell's own".

expectations.text: Separates badge eligibility from badge display, assigning eligibility to the app-review process and display to the listing rulebook
expectations.evidence: "Eligibility belongs to the review process (`app-marketplace-review`). Display rules belong to the listing rulebook."

expectations.text: Recommends a dedicated trust surface - a listing tab or section physically separate from the marketing copy
expectations.evidence: "Dedicated trust tab (default)... Physically separate from the marketing copy."

expectations.text: Specifies what that surface carries: data-storage location, earned badges, and compliance certifications
expectations.evidence: "Data-storage location, earned Tidewell badge with review date and status, vendor compliance certifications."

expectations.text: Pairs it with a written currency rule: a lapsed badge comes down, with a stated grace period
expectations.evidence: Lapse sequence with a 30-day grace period; chip and badge come down at grace expiry.

expectations.text: Describes an inline badge chip in search results as a complement to the trust surface rather than a substitute, because it asserts trust without the substantiating detail a diligence buyer needs
expectations.evidence: "Cheap complement only. It asserts trust but doesn't substantiate it."

expectations.text: Names renewal-linked display automation - display wired to eligibility data so a lapsed badge disappears without human intervention - as the highest-effort option that loses the efficiency ranking
expectations.evidence: "manual takedown is the default. Wire badge display to review-program eligibility data... highest-effort option."

expectations.text: States the condition that promotes it: badges carrying quantitative, lapsable thresholds on a renewal cycle
expectations.evidence: "once badges carry quantitative, lapsable thresholds."

expectations.text: Classifies the vendor-embeddable off-marketplace badge as marketing reach rather than listing trust
expectations.evidence: "Vendor-embeddable badge: optional, but it's marketing, not trust."

expectations.text: Requires a brand-usage rulebook for that badge covering use-as-provided, minimum clear space, size parity with competing badges, and a mandatory link back to the listing
expectations.evidence: Use as provided; clear space of one-quarter badge height; size equal or larger; mandatory link back.

expectations.text: Notes that running no badge program at all is a legitimate architecture rather than an oversight
expectations.evidence: Not stated. It assumes a hybrid or certified-tier model.
